guideTitle: 6 Best Electric Bath Lift Chairs in 2026
metaTitle: Best Electric Bath Lift Chairs in 2026
metaDescription: Six electric bath lift chairs compared by frame design, battery routine, waterproof rating, remote type and emergency stop, for safe powered lifting.
introParagraphs: An electric bath lift chair is a small machine that lives in a wet room, and that combination deserves some scrutiny. Inside the plastic and aluminum there is a motor, a battery, a controller and a mechanism that raises and lowers a person, all sitting on a tub floor by suction. How each part is built and protected decides whether the lift is a quiet, reliable helper or an anxious piece of equipment, so the technical details are worth reading carefully rather than skimming past.

The six picks here are all battery powered and waterproof, with different mechanisms. The PELEGON is a motorized scissor lift on an X-shape frame with a wired three-button remote, the PERLECARE and PPOLB are foldable chairs with cordless remotes and 308 lb ratings, and the VOCIC AX10 adds wheels and two suction cup types. The Mobi-Lift uses an industrial steel rod frame with a foam seat and foldable wings, and the Bellavita is a dual-column reclining lift with floating controls.

We evaluated each from listing specs and buyer feedback, not from hands-on lab work. For a powered device in water we weigh safety features first: emergency stop, waterproof rating, stable base and a battery that does not surprise you, and we treat every rating as a specification to read carefully, not a promise about how the lift will behave in a particular tub.

products.name: PELEGON Electric Lift Chair, 2-in-1 Floor Lift and Bath Lift, 300 lb
products.description:
The PELEGON uses a motorized scissor mechanism on a reinforced X-shape frame, with a suction cup base, side flaps and slip-resistant seat padding. A simple wired hand control has three buttons: Up, Down and Emergency Stop. The listing gives an IP68 waterproof rating for bath use, a 300 lb capacity and a folded size of 27.5 by 6 inches, with one-click assembly.

A scissor lift raises the seat vertically on crossing arms, which is a compact and well-understood mechanism. The X-shape frame adds rigidity, and the side flaps bridge the gap to the tub ledge. The wired remote means there is no remote battery to run flat, though the cord needs care around water.

It sits in the middle of the price range. Compared with the cordless chairs it trades wireless freedom for a controller that cannot go out of charge. Choose it for a simple scissor mechanism and a three-button remote. Before the first bath, check each button with the lift empty and dry, including the Emergency Stop, and keep the cord clear of the water. Fold it only when dry and dry the cord and remote after bathing.
products.bestFor: Users and caregivers who want a simple scissor lift and a wired three-button control.
pros: Scissor lift on an X-shape frame
Up, Down and Emergency Stop buttons
cons: Wired remote has a cord near water

products.name: PERLECARE Electric Chair Lift for Elderly, Bath Lift for Tub, 308 lb
products.description:
The PERLECARE puts battery performance first, with a high-capacity rechargeable battery that the listing says delivers over 50 full lift-and-lower cycles on a single charge. The seat height runs from 2.3 to 18.9 inches, the backrest adjusts from 140 to 93 degrees and a remote control runs the lift. It has an IP68 waterproof rating and carries 308 lb on a six-point stable base.

The upgraded one-piece integrated locking buckle is meant to reduce breakage risk compared with multi-clip or detachable structures, which is a design detail that matters when a frame folds and unfolds repeatedly. The quick-fold design reduces the chair to 6.4 inches in thickness for storage. A long battery life means fewer charging chores and fewer surprises mid-bath.

It sits in the middle of the price range. Compared with the PPOLB it has similar specs and a longer-described battery. Choose it for battery endurance and a one-piece lock. Charge it before the first bath, test the lock after folding and unfolding it a few times and press the suction base onto a clean tub floor. Dry the lift thoroughly before it is folded, and check the buckle for wear.
products.bestFor: Daily bathers who want fewer charging chores and a sturdy one-piece lock.
cons: No emergency stop mentioned in the material we reviewed

products.name: PPOLB Electric Chair Lift for Bath and Floor, 308 lb
products.description:
The PPOLB pairs an IPX8 waterproof rating with six heavy-duty suction cups and a rechargeable system that the listing says charges fully in 2.5 hours and delivers over 50 lift cycles. A remote offers one-touch Lift, Lower and Emergency Stop. The seat height runs from 2.3 to 18.9 inches, and the backrest tilts from 140 to 93 degrees as the seat rises. It carries 308 lb and comes with a 3-year warranty.

The warranty term is the longest in this lineup, which matters for a powered device with a battery and a motor. The emergency stop is a feature to test before the first bath. The suction base anchors on tile, marble or hardwood, and the widened seat has body-contouring grooves.

It sits in the middle of the price range. Compared with the PERLECARE it adds an emergency stop and a longer warranty. Choose it for the warranty and the stop button. Test the Emergency Stop empty, then with the user seated and a helper present. Charge the remote on a schedule, and check the suction cups for grit before each bath.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want an emergency stop and the longest stated warranty.

products.name: VOCIC Electric Bath Lift for Tub AX10, 300 lb
products.description:
The VOCIC AX10 is rated IP68 with a fully encased motor and sealed remote connections, and the listing states that it allows safe submersion for approximately 40 minutes. A rechargeable cordless hand control avoids an electrical cord near water. It includes two types of suction cups, six of each, to match different tub and floor surfaces, and built-in wheels let a caregiver roll the lift into place.

The seat height range of 2.9 to 19.7 inches reaches higher than most electric chairs, and it folds with no assembly. The listing says it also helps with rising from the floor and offers a one-year after-sales service. The specific submersion time is a useful detail, since many listings state only a rating.

It sits in the lower-middle of the price range. Compared with the PELEGON it is cordless and wheeled. Choose it for mobility and suction options. Try both suction cup types on your tub floor to see which holds better, and test the wheels on the bathroom floor. Charge the remote regularly and dry the lift before it is stored.
products.bestFor: Caregivers who move the lift and need suction options for the tub.
pros: Stated submersion time of about 40 minutes

products.name: Mobi-Lift Electric Bath Lift Chair, 300 lb
products.description:
The Mobi-Lift uses a high-strength industrial grade steel rod frame, weighs about 29 lb and carries 300 lb, with an upgraded foam-padded seat. The listing says it raises up to 20 inches to help the user stand, has an IPX8 waterproof standard and uses six suction cups for stability in the tub. It runs on rechargeable batteries that take about 3 hours to charge and work for 15 hours.

Two foldable side wings help the user move from the ground to the lift and slide into place, and the seat cushion offers an attachable swivel seat to help the user get in and out of the tub more easily. The listing notes that the indicator light will not light up while the hand control is charging, a small detail worth knowing. It is designed for the tub but can be used outside it.

It sits in the lower-middle of the price range. Compared with the aluminum chairs it is heavier but has a steel frame and a padded seat. Choose it for a steel frame, a padded seat and a swivel option. Check the indicator light behavior when you charge the hand control, as the listing warns, and test the side wings and the swivel cushion if you use it. Dry the foam seat after each bath.
products.bestFor: Users who want a steel frame, a padded seat and an optional swivel cushion.

products.name: Drive Medical Bellavita Dive Reclining Electric Bath Lift Chair
products.description:
The Bellavita uses a patented dual-column construction rated to 310 lb for stable support during the rise and the lowering. Patented 3D suction feet adhere the seat to the tub floor, and floating hand controls with large, color-coded buttons stay on the water's surface so the user can reach them from within the bath. The seat height adjusts from 2.6 to 18.9 inches, and the backrest reclines 50 degrees.

The floating control is the standout feature: a control that floats cannot sink out of reach, and large color-coded buttons make the functions clear to a user who is nervous or wet. An open seat cutout improves access for washing. The lift weighs only 10.89 lb and the listing gives its dimensions.

It sits near the top of the price range. Compared with the scissor and X-frame chairs it uses two columns and has the best control design. Choose it for floating controls and a reclined soak. Check that the floating control floats the right way up and that its buttons respond, and practice reaching it from the seated position. Wipe the open seat clean and dry the lift after bathing.
products.bestFor: Users who want controls they can always reach and a reclined soak.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The PELEGON uses a scissor lift on an X-shape frame, the Bellavita a dual-column design, the Mobi-Lift a steel rod frame and the PERLECARE, PPOLB and VOCIC foldable chair frames. Scissor and column designs have different failure points: joints in a scissor, sleeves in a column. Choose a mechanism that the listing describes clearly, and watch for any play or noise during the first week of use. A mechanism that you can see and understand is easier to inspect than one hidden inside a housing.

The PERLECARE, PELEGON and VOCIC list IP68, the PPOLB and Mobi-Lift IPX8. IP68 and IPX8 are both ratings for continuous submersion, with the details set by the maker, and the VOCIC states about 40 minutes. Read what the maker says about submersion depth and time. Never use a lift with a damaged cover, seal or connector. Ask the maker what the rating covers if the listing is vague.

The PPOLB offers one-touch Lift, Lower and Emergency Stop, the PELEGON has an Emergency Stop button, and the Bellavita's floating controls have color-coded buttons. A stop control is a basic safety feature, and a remote that can be reached is as important as one that works. Test the stop with the lift empty before the first bath. Treat a stop button as something to test every few weeks, not just once.

The PERLECARE and PPOLB list over 50 cycles per charge, the PPOLB charges in 2.5 hours, and the Mobi-Lift needs about 3 hours to charge and runs about 15 hours. Longer endurance means fewer chores. Know the low-battery signal, keep the charger away from water and charge on a schedule. Write the charge date on a calendar if the user is likely to forget.

The PPOLB and Mobi-Lift use six suction cups, the VOCIC two types of six each and the Bellavita 3D suction feet. Suction needs a clean, smooth tub floor and fails on textured surfaces. Test the lift before the user sits, and replace worn suction parts. A lift that moves is a lift to retire.

Ratings are 300 lb on the PELEGON, VOCIC and Mobi-Lift, 308 lb on the PERLECARE and PPOLB and 310 lb on the Bellavita. Weights run from 10.89 lb on the Bellavita to about 29 lb on the Mobi-Lift. A lift that is hard to lift and store stays in the tub, which is bad for the seat and the battery. A lift that is hard to store may be left in a damp tub.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mechanism and structure
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the PELEGON's scissor lift, the Bellavita's dual columns, the Mobi-Lift's steel rod frame and the folding frames of the PERLECARE, PPOLB and VOCIC. We credited descriptions that explain how the structure resists loosening. A mechanism that is clearly described earns more trust than a bare feature list.

howWeEvaluated.title: Water protection
howWeEvaluated.description: We read IP68 and IPX8 ratings and noted the VOCIC's stated submersion time. A clearly described rating scored higher than a bare label. A stated submersion time made a rating more useful.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls and safety
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for emergency stops and reachable controls, crediting the PPOLB's stop, the PELEGON's stop and the Bellavita's floating buttons. A reachable control is a safety feature, not a luxury.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery routine
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared charge times and cycles: 2.5 hours and over 50 lifts on the PPOLB, over 50 cycles on the PERLECARE and 3 hours for 15 hours of use on the Mobi-Lift. A battery that surprises the user is a hazard in itself.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stability and handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered suction designs, weights and folding. The Bellavita's light weight and the PERLECARE's fold stood out. Handling decides whether the lift gets used and stored properly.

faq.q: Is it safe to use electric equipment in a bathtub?
faq.a: These lifts are designed for it, with waterproof ratings and battery power instead of mains. IP68 and IPX8 are ratings for submersion, and the maker sets the details. Follow the instructions, keep remotes charged and stop using a lift with damage.

faq.q: What is the difference between IP68 and IPX8?
faq.a: Both indicate protection against continuous submersion, with the exact depth and time set by the manufacturer. IP68 also states dust protection. The VOCIC states about 40 minutes of submersion for its IP68 rating. Read the maker's conditions.

faq.q: How long will the battery last?
faq.a: The PERLECARE and PPOLB list over 50 lift cycles per charge, and the Mobi-Lift lists about 15 hours of use per charge. Charging times are 2.5 to 3 hours. Charge on a schedule and watch the low-battery signal.

faq.q: What happens if the battery dies mid-bath?
faq.a: The lift may stop at its current height, so keep a helper nearby and know the maker's guidance for manual release or help. Do not rely on the lift alone if the battery is low. Charge before each bathing session if in doubt.

faq.q: How do I test the emergency stop?
faq.a: With the lift empty and dry, raise it a little, then press the stop and confirm it halts. Repeat with the user seated and dressed, and a helper beside them. Do this before the first bath.

faq.q: Can I use an electric lift for floor recovery?
faq.a: Several listings describe floor lifting as a secondary use, but a bath lift is not an emergency service or a medical device. If someone has fallen and is hurt, call for help. Use the lift only as the maker directs.

faq.q: What should I check on the lift each week?
faq.a: Look at the suction cups for grit and wear, test the controls and the stop, check the frame joints or buckles for play and make sure the battery is charged. Dry the lift after every bath. If anything has changed or feels loose, take the lift out of use until it is fixed.
